validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: real, FERC-certificated project. Docket CP15-16: Transco's application was filed Nov 18, 2014 (govinfo FR-2014-12-11/2014-29054, an NGA sec.7 application for 43.5 mi of looping + 88,500 hp compression, 'all in Alabama', to lease 1,131,730 Dth/d to Sabal Trail); certificated by FERC's Feb 2, 2016 order (154 FERC P61,080, cited in the 2021 extension notice). CLASSIFICATION: correct -- this is an interstate transmission-pipeline looping expansion of Transco's existing FERC-regulated mainline (EIA workbook: Pipeline Type='Interstate', Authority='FERC'), not a gathering/feeder line. DUPLICATE: not a duplicate of anything in this 44-row roster -- Phase 1 (in service Jul 2017) and Phase 2 (in service May 2020, per Williams' May 1 2020 press release cited on the wiki page) are separate GEM PIDs already swept in a different batch ('Phases 1-2 swept, batch 2' per orchestrator note); this row (P2545) is specifically Phase 3 only: ~13 mi of 42-in looping = the Butler Loop (Choctaw County) + Autauga Loop (Autauga/Chilton Counties). Capacity arithmetic corroborates the split: FR notice states the WHOLE project leases 1,131,730 Dth/d to Sabal Trail; industry reporting gives Phase 1 = 818,000 Dth/d and Phase 2 = 206,000 Dth/d, leaving ~107,730 Dth/d for Phase 3 -- matches the recorded 106 MMcf/d closely. ATTRIBUTION: Owner/Operator = Transco (Transcontinental Gas Pipe Line Company, LLC), 100%, uncontested -- named as applicant in the 2014 FERC application and as 'Pipeline Operator Name' in the EIA workbook. LOCATION: the routes-repo geometry for P2545 is two disjoint short segments -- one near Butler/Choctaw County AL (approx. -88.17 to -88.25 lon, 32.10-32.13 lat) and one near the Autauga/Chilton County AL area (approx. -86.60 to -86.72 lon, 32.67-32.72 lat) -- consistent with the Butler Loop and Autauga Loop respectively, confirming StartState/Province=Alabama and EndState/Province=Alabama are correct (not a route-vs-sheet mismatch; not one of the orchestrator's flagged mismatch cases and I found none here). EIA-follow-up delta pass (2026-09-10): the classification cite (Pipeline Type='Interstate', Authority='FERC', Project Type='Expansion') is re-pointed to the dated Aug-2026 EIA release, sheet 'Natural Gas Pipeline Projects', row 63, replacing the undated EIA-NaturalGasPipelineProjects.xlsx pointer per the follow-up's standing instruction.

validity.recommendation: Verify StartYear1 and SegmentCost against the FERC certificate / a current Williams project fact sheet before pasting -- both are disputed by sources found in this sweep.
validity.researcher_notes: StartYear1: the sheet records 2026 (single year); EIA's Natural Gas Pipeline Projects workbook, last updated for this row 2026-07-22, records Year In Service Date = 2027 and Status = 'On Hold' -- and its own Notes field says 'FERC granted 2-year extension to 5/1/2023; lack of subsequent filing implies project has been postponed or canceled.' The gem.wiki table cell itself already shows a range '2026-2027' with a footnote 'Originally 2023', so the sheet's single StartYear1=2026 undersells even the wiki's own uncertainty, and as of this Sept-2026 sweep the 2026 date has already passed with no in-service or construction news found. I searched FERC's elibrary docket page structure, SEC EDGAR (Williams' FY2021, FY2023 and FY2025 10-Ks: zero hits for 'Hillabee' in any of them -- likely just below their materiality threshold, so absence is not conclusive either way), and trade press (NGI, OGJ, Hart Energy, P&GJ) for any 2022-2026 construction/completion/cancellation news and found none past the 2021 FERC extension request. Recommend 2027 (or leave blank pending the sponsor's current fact sheet) rather than 2026, and see status_reviews for the fuller status picture. SegmentCost: the sheet/EIA both show a single $15,000,000 figure for the combined 13-mi Phase 3 scope. A July 2017 Williams-sourced trade article (industrialinfo.com) itemizes the two loops separately at the pre-construction-estimate stage: Butler Loop $15 million (5.3 mi) + Autauga Loop $20 million (7.5 mi) = $35 million combined -- exactly double the recorded figure, and the $15M portion alone matches Butler Loop only, suggesting the sheet/EIA number may capture just one of the two loops rather than the combined Phase-3 total that Length (13 mi) and Capacity (106 MMcf/d) represent. I could not reach the actual FERC certificate's cost table to resolve which figure (if either) is the final certificated cost: the only copy of the Feb 2016 order I located (a scanned mirror on saj.usace.army.mil) 403s to both a research and a browser user-agent. Leaving the corrected value blank rather than asserting $35M, since the 2017 figures were pre-construction estimates that may have changed by certification; flagging for a researcher with FERC eLibrary access to check 154 FERC P61,080 directly. Searched FERC's docket history for CP15-16 post-2021 (elibrary's own search UI is not scriptable; relied on Federal Register/govinfo notices and secondary docket summaries, none dated after the April 2021 extension request), SEC EDGAR full-text of Williams' FY2021, FY2023 and FY2025 10-Ks (zero hits for 'Hillabee' in any -- the project is evidently below Williams' 10-K materiality threshold, so this is not itself evidence of completion or cancellation), and trade press (NGI, OGJ, Hart Energy, P&GJ, S&P Global) for any dated news after the June 2021 FERC order granting the extension to May 1, 2023. Found nothing newer than that 2021 order describing this specific 13-mi/Butler+Autauga scope. The newest dated evidence is EIA's Natural Gas Pipeline Projects workbook, whose row for 'Hillabee Expansion Phase 3' was itself last updated 2026-07-22 and lists Status='On Hold' with the note: 'FERC granted 2-year extension to 5/1/2023; lack of subsequent filing implies project has been postponed or canceled.' That is an affirmative, dated (2026-07), LITERAL classification from EIA, not merely silence, so I am treating it as a 'change' rather than a bare dormancy-only 'stale' call -- but since EIA's own reasoning is itself an inference from the absence of a subsequent FERC filing (not a sponsor announcement or a docket order), and the underlying dormancy math also clears the 2-year no-progress threshold (last regulatory deadline May 1, 2023 -> now Sept 2026, >3 years with zero subsequent filing found), ShelvedCancelledType is set to 'inferred' with no fabricated ref for the inference itself, per standing rule. Recommend Status='shelved' (not 'cancelled' -- the >=4-year cancelled threshold from the last concrete milestone, May 2023, is not yet reached) and StartYear1 should not be relied on as an active target (see the separate spec concern on StartYear1/SegmentCost). If a researcher gets FERC eLibrary docket access for CP15-16, checking for any filing after April 2021 would resolve this more directly than EIA's inference, and would also supply the FERC-origin second source this unit still owes.
